newsitem.title: USA: Odwalla urges industry halt fresh apple juice sales.
newsitem.headline: Odwalla urges industry halt fresh apple juice sales.

text.p: The head of a company whose apple juice has been linked to an outbreak of food poisoning recommended Monday that all producers stop selling unpasteurized apple juice until the industry finds a way to assure the juice is safe.
"We think it is not prudent for any fresh producer of apple juices to continue to have the products on shelves at this time," Odwalla Inc chief executive Stephen Williamson said at a news conference.

Odwalla apple juice has been linked to an outbreak of E.coli in several western states and Canada that has sickened 50 people and claimed the life of one young child. Odwalla pulled 16 products -- any containing apple juice -- from store shelves after the first reported case in October.
But a U.S. Food and Drug Administration inspection of the Odwalla plant in Dinuba, California, completed Friday found no presence of E.coli, Odwalla executives said Monday.

But two microbiologists retained by Odwalla as advisers, said it appeared there was no conclusive way to test for the presence in juice of the particular strain of E.coli at the root of the recent outbreak.

According to Dr. Michael Doyle of the University of Georgia's Department of Food Science and Technology and Dr. Ranzell Nickelson of the Red Mesa Microbiology food quality consulting firm, current industry practices for washing and processing apples into juice appear inadequate to assure the E.coli has been eliminated.
Because of these findings Odwalla executives said Monday they would lead an industry effort to find new ways to process and test fresh apple juice.
The FDA's findings confirmed "this is not just an Odwalla problem, but an issue for the entire industry," Williamson said.
Williamson said Odwalla itself will not make apple juice for the foreseeable future until it figures out a process to assure the juice doesn't contain any harmful bacteria.
